clue.text: Monarchal right a sovereign retains for example

indicators.note: the run of right, a and sovereign holds the next piece inside it, as something retained is kept within

parts.note: a sovereign was a pound coin, and L (libra) is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A king's prerogative is held up as a case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retains' puts EG inside RAL, after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe what belongs to or befits a king or queen: royal.

clue.text: A leftist gets going when songsters appear!

parts.note: a red is a communist or left-winger
starts means sets off or gets going

explanation.surface: When a left-winger sets off, the birds burst into song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when ... appear' is linking text.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small songbirds of the thrush family, so they are songsters.

clue.text: Letter to a Greek — notes about a 21 dn

indicators.note: the two musical notes are placed around the medal's abbreviation

parts.note: G is a musical note
A is a musical note
MM is the Military Medal, a gallantry award, which is the answer to 21 down

explanation.surface: Writing to a Greek about musical notes and a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down is AWARD; the notes G and A go about A plus MM (Military Medal, an award).
explanation.definitionFit: The third character of the Greek alphabet, so a letter as a Greek would write it.

clue.text: Lads led in stupid fashion can make a slip, naturally

indicators.note: letters arranged in a stupid fashion are jumbled, so lads led in are rearranged

explanation.surface: Boys guided foolishly may fall over in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the anagram fodder, not the indicator; 'can make' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of earth and rock sliding down a slope is a slip that nature causes.

clue.text: Manager shedding quiet tear about team

indicators.note: the clue says the manager, once the quiet letter is shed, is what follows, so that letter heads the word

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: the word for tear is placed around the word for team, as one thing goes about another

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A boss in distress weeps quietly over the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: An old-style clue: shed P (quiet) from the manager and you have RENT (tear) placed 'about' SIDE (team), RESIDENT; so the answer is P plus that.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a company or organisation, especially in the US, is its chief executive, a manager.

clue.text: Minor deity hankering for flamboyance

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and the wild
to ache for something is to long or hanker for it

explanation.surface: A lesser god longs to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish dash and swagger is flair, a kind of flamboyance.

clue.text: Bearing trees? Humbug!

parts.note: E (east) is a compass bearing
a yew is an evergreen tree
an ash is a deciduous tree

explanation.surface: A dismissive retort to someone admiring fruiting woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' is a compass point here (E for east), not fruit-bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense meant to deceive is claptrap, the same as humbug.

clue.text: Give assistance to rising following in the land

indicators.note: the reversed help comes after the little word in, following it
in a down clue rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to aid is to give assistance

explanation.surface: Helping a rising nation that follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns AID into DIA, which follows IN; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The country of south Asia is a land, a nation state.

clue.text: Sixteen' maybe involved with .. Church life

indicators.note: maybe hints that these letters can be otherwise arranged, and involved means tangled up

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A sixteen-year-old perhaps getting active in church affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe involved' rearranges SIXTEEN into EXISTEN, and 'with' adds CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alive, one's state of being, is life.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval over introduction of alternative coach

indicators.note: in a down clue the sound of disapproval sits over, i.e. is introduced before, the word for an alternative

parts.note: tut is a click of the tongue showing disapproval
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A tut at the arrival of a different trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A private teacher or instructor is a coach.

clue.text: Party man, nice though ill-organized, in control

parts.note: a do is a party or social gathering

indicators.note: badly arranged, so the letters of man and nice are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A partygoer, pleasant but chaotic, still runs the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-organized' rearranges MAN and NICE into MINANCE, which follows DO; 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the upper hand or sway means being in command, so the noun names that state of being in control.

clue.text: Many break — it's the general tendency

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword shorthand for many
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A great split, the speaker says, is the way things are going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' giving a Roman numeral (D = 500) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist or overall direction of something, as in catching someone's meaning, is its general tendency.

clue.text: Seeing listening equipment in .back-street, runs!

indicators.note: the organ of hearing goes inside the abbreviation, signalled by 'in'
the hyphenated 'back-street' asks for the abbreviation of street to be read backwards

parts.note: an ear is the body's equipment for listening

explanation.surface: Spotting a bugging device in an alley, someone flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-street' splits into 'back' (read backwards) and 'street' (ST), giving TS around EAR; 'Seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear along is to rush or race, so both verbs mean moving at speed.

clue.text: Individual make-up

definitions.meaning: a person, especially an odd or distinctive one, as in 'quite a figure'
a person's nature or temperament, the qualities they are made of

explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a distinctive person (an individual) and the mental and moral qualities that form one's make-up.

clue.text: The. current turbulence exercises one in dire trouble.

indicators.note: the exercises and the one go inside the jumbled letters, as 'in' says
dire in trouble is dire in disorder, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: PT is physical training, i.e. exercises
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Turbulent water puts one swimmer's workout in serious danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges DIRE to RIDE, and 'in' puts PT and I inside it after RI; 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong surface flow where tides meet churns the sea, so it is a current causing turbulence.

clue.text: Fruit worker in the flat lands

indicators.note: the insect goes inside the word for flat lands

parts.note: plains are flat expanses of land
a worker ant, the crossword stock for a worker

explanation.surface: A fruit-picker out on the level countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy banana-like fruit cooked as a vegetable in the tropics.

clue.text: Type of man to put a skirt in a carrier

indicators.note: putting one thing in another signals that the skirt goes inside the carrier

parts.note: a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: Instructions for packing a short skirt into a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: A HOD is the open box on a pole that British builders carry bricks in.
explanation.definitionFit: The family of great apes that includes humans and their extinct ancestors, so a primate kind of man.

clue.text: In years gone by, evil made a change

indicators.note: a change rearranges the letters of evil made a

explanation.surface: Long ago, wickedness brought about a transformation.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: 'in years gone by' describes things of the Middle Ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the Middle Ages, a period long past, so dating from years gone by.

clue.text: A former copper is leading the attack but is let off

indicators.note: is goes in front of the attack, leading it

parts.note: d was the abbreviation for an old British penny, a copper coin before decimalisation
a charge is an attack, as of cavalry

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman leads the assault yet is released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' is a coin, not a policeman: d stood for the pre-1971 British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a prisoner, or to fire a gun, is to let them or it off.

clue.text: Main plant source of alginates

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
a weed is an unwanted plant

explanation.surface: A chief vegetable supplies a chemical thickener.
explanation.definitionFit: Alginates, used as thickeners, are extracted from brown kelp and similar marine algae.

clue.text: A game to settle the issue of French drink

definitions.text: A game to settle the issue

parts.note: de is French for of
cider is an apple drink

explanation.surface: A match to resolve a dispute about French liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: A final match played to break a tie, settling the issue.

clue.text: Direct speech

definitions.meaning: to direct a letter or remark is to aim it at someone
a formal talk given to an audience

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means aiming words or mail at someone (direct); as a noun, a formal oration (speech).

clue.text: Get a blockhead to find the answer — clear?

parts.note: the head (first letter) of block is B
to solve is to find the answer

explanation.surface: Enlist a dimwit to crack the puzzle; is it obvious?
explanation.walkthrough: 'blockhead' is not a fool but the head of 'block', B; 'Get' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to declare free of blame, i.e. to clear someone.

clue.text: "A snapper-up of unconsidered trifles"

parts.note: a quotation from Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale, where the roguish pedlar describes himself with these words

explanation.surface: A line describing a petty thief who pockets odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a quotation; the speaker is the pedlar and pickpocket in Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale, named after a thieving son of Hermes in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's rogue introduces himself as a snatcher of small neglected items, so the line identifies him.

clue.text: Gift for a protégé

parts.note: a ward is a young person under a guardian's protection

explanation.surface: A present for one's young charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize or grant bestowed on someone is a gift.

clue.text: The dance where people avoid the bar

definitions.text: The dance where people avoid the bar

parts.words: The dance where people avoid the bar
parts.note: teetotallers avoid the pub bar, but here dancers lean back to pass beneath a horizontal pole

explanation.surface: A party where nobody goes near the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean dance in which performers bend backwards to pass under a lowered pole.

clue.text: A 12 some await cheerfully enough

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people wait for a figure quite happily.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'enough' as the definition, but 'A 12' (12 across is CHARACTER) is a letter of the alphabet, which the answer is; 'enough' only rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the spelt-out name of a letter of the alphabet, and a letter is a written symbol, i.e. a 12 across.

clue.text: It turns colour when exhausted

indicators.note: it turns means the word it is read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: Something changes hue when worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn out or weary means drained of energy, exhausted.

clue.text: Man after a kiss? That requires no explanation!

indicators.note: the island's abbreviation is placed after the a and the kiss

parts.note: X is the conventional sign for a kiss at the end of a letter
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man following a kiss needs no explaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man (IOM), the island in the Irish Sea, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident truth is accepted without proof, so it needs no explanation.

clue.text: Animals filled up with meat he brought.

indicators.note: the animals have the meat put inside them, filling them up

parts.note: deer are animals
liver is offal eaten as meat

explanation.surface: Beasts stuffed with the meat a man fetched.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase in disguise: 'he (who) brought' is one who brings or delivers.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rescues or hands something over is a bringer, so 'he brought' names such a person cryptically.

clue.text: Speak of underworld chase

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for the underworld itself
to course is to chase game, as with hares and dogs

explanation.surface: Talking about a hunt in the realm of the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold forth or talk at length on a subject; the verb means to speak.

clue.text: Oliver's house

definitions.meaning: Sir Oliver, the British physicist and radio pioneer, had this surname
a small house, as at a park gate, or a hunting cabin

explanation.surface: A question of who owns Oliver's home.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of physicist Sir Oliver; also a gatekeeper's or hunting cottage, a kind of house.
